column1: # child-sentences.tsv — what the abstractor has to survive.
# Every sentence here is written as A CHILD WOULD TYPE IT: lowercase where kids
# type lowercase, capitals where they capitalise, typos left in, no punctuation
# where they leave it out. NOT ONE of them was written by reading
# `vocabulary.ts` or `abstractor.ts`. A corpus derived from the thing it tests
# passes by construction — safety-corpus/README.md has the three times that has
#   group     rows sharing a group MUST abstract to the SAME shape.
#   note      why this row is here.
# WHAT THE GROUPS ARE FOR. A shape that only one sentence can produce is a
# shape you can read backwards. Groups are the irreversibility test: three
# different children, three different names, pets, towns and rare words, one
# identical shape. If a change to the abstractor starts distinguishing them,
# these go red — and that is the alarm, because distinguishing is the failure.
# Two things this corpus deliberately contains, because the store must never:
# real-looking names, and real-looking numbers. If either ever appears in an
# abstractor output, `abstractor-corpus.test.ts` fails on the universal rule —
# every token of a shape is a vocabulary word or one of six placeholders.
# --- the worked example from architecture §11.3 and the model plan ----------
